description: Pins the NTV7 vault.meta generation: the NTV6 frame byte for byte, with the three recovery-phrase wrap fields structurally zero and a fixed 1208-byte person envelope sealing root_key to the owner's person key. A conformant port parses the frame, must refuse a non-zero phrase-wrap field and any length other than 445 + roster_len + 1208, and must open the person wrap only under the recipient key and the frame's own items_key_id. `parse_fail` cases are expected to return the one non-distinguishing invalid-metadata result. Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_vault_meta_ntv7_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored --nocapture`.

cases.description: A full NTV7 frame: base with the phrase wrap zeroed, the NTV6 tail (group-key package, epoch 1, sealed roster), then the person envelope sealed to the fixture owner. parse then re-serialize must reproduce these bytes exactly, and the tail fields must be read back at their offsets.

The same frame with its magic relabelled NTV6. An NTV6 reader treats the tail as ending there, so NTV7 must be its own magic and this is the case that holds a reader to the magic rather than to the layout.

A byte written into the recovery SALT (offset 49). NTV7 retires the phrase wrap, so a frame that still carries any byte of it is structurally invalid rather than a vault whose saved phrase may or may not still work.
A byte written into the recovery wrap NONCE (offset 153). Same structural rule as the salt.
A byte written into the recovery-wrapped root_key (offset 177). Same structural rule: the third and last field the phrase wrap occupied.
One byte appended after the person envelope. The frame length is fixed at 445 + roster_len + 1208, so trailing bytes are a rejection and not an extension point.
cases.informational_reason: trailing bytes after the person envelope

cases.description: group_key_epoch forced to 0 (bytes 433..441). An epoch of zero is not a valid group-key generation in any NTV6-derived frame.

The owner's deterministic keypair (from the three seeds) opens the person envelope to the vault's root_key, under the frame's own items_key_id. A port derives the hybrid wrap key from the ML-KEM decapsulation and the Ed25519 static DH, then AEAD-opens under role 'person-wrap-root-key' bound to its fingerprint and that items_key_id.
One ML-KEM ciphertext bit flipped. The PQ half decapsulates to a different secret, so the hybrid wrap key differs and the AEAD refuses.
One nonce bit flipped. The nonce is keystream input for XChaCha20-Poly1305 as well as CTX commitment input, so a changed nonce is a different keystream and a failed tag.

The AAD's vault binding: the SAME frame opened with another vault's items_key_id. This is the case that pins why items_key_id is in the AAD at all; without it a root_key sealed for one vault would open in another of the same owner.
